Subject: Post-cutover issues: latency up, hallucinations increasing

Hi Monica —

We did the model cutover to v4.1 + int8 profile this morning (09:00 local) per the plan. Since ~10:40 were seeing: p95/99 latency up ~2.5x, tail-timeouts, and a noticeable rise in output incoherence (short hallucinations on several user prompts). Throughput has dropped ~30% under the same QPS. This is customer-facing and were starting to receive tickets.

I attached a short log excerpt and a latency plot. Can you confirm whether you rolled any runtime kernel or KV-cache change with v4.1? We need immediate mitigation steps — our SLA is at risk.

Attached: support_log_20270610.txt, latency_plot_20270610.png

— Alex

Appreciate the quick report and attachments. Ive asked SRE and the CS patch team to triage immediately. Short term mitigation were pushing right away:
- Pin traffic for Cardwell to the v4.0.12 variant (compatibility fallback) and route new sessions to that variant while we investigate v4.1.
- Throttle concurrency for the v4.1 pool by 40% to reduce tail contention.
- Enable aggressive prefix/KV-cache warmup for hot endpoints.

Ben / Priyom: confirm when the pin+throttle is live and whether we should rollback quant profile to fp16 for v4.1 candidates. If we do rollback, well need an agreed outage window (expect short blip).

Subject: Re: Post-cutover issues: latency up, hallucinations increasing

Monica / team —

Short update and proposed runbook (executing now):
1) Confirmed that v4.1 uses the new int8 kernel set plus a more aggressive KV-eviction policy. That combination likely explains increased tail latency and throughput compression.
2) Immediate: pin Cardwell traffic to v4.0.12 as Monica requested (in progress). This preserves customer traffic while we validate v4.1.
3) Mitigation path A (fast): revert runtime quant flag for v4.1 to prefer_fp16_kernels=true and redeploy a small canary subset of nodes (15%). This reduces token-cost savings but restores stability. Needs 20 minutes.
4) Mitigation path B (safer): keep v4.1 int8 but adjust KV-eviction threshold and increase capacity for hot shards; longer (1-2 hours) and riskier with autoscaler churn.
5) Collect 30 minutes of traces + token-level logs (already requested). Ben to provide roll-forward timestamp and confirm whether route-pin completed.

Im recommending path A for immediate restoration; we can re-evaluate after traces.

— Priyom
Lead CS Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Canary rollback of v4.1 quant flag to prefer_fp16_kernels=true started at 10:20 PDT and completed on the 15% canary pool at 10:39 PDT. Canary showed ~20% lower p95 compared to int8 nodes and no output coherence regressions in sampled traces.
- We have collected token-level traces and error stacks; attached one trimmed log and the latency plot.

Next steps:
- Full rollback of v4.1 quant flag to fp16 on the remaining pool scheduled at 12:00 PDT today (planned 5-minute impact window; we will post on status and coordinate).
- Post-rollback, we will run an automated regression harness against Cardwell's supplied prompt set and send a quality report within 2 hours.
- Ops will prepare a postmortem that includes kernel-selection diffs, KV-eviction deltas, and recommended permanent config for Cardwell (likely: stick to fp16 kernels for now; re-evaluate int8 after targeted perf tests).
